newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer sees '96 losses in all sports units.
newsitem.headline: Amer sees '96 losses in all sports units.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said on Thursday sales at its largest division, Wilson sports, would be flat this year and it expected losses from all three of its major sports equipment units.
"(Wilson's) full year sales are expected to remain flat compared to 1995," Amer said in a statement. Overall, sport goods made up 76 percent of Amer's January-August net sales.
Amer, which earlier warned it would be clearly loss-making in 1996, said all its three big-name brand units -- Wilson, MacGregor and Atomic -- would be loss-making this year.
Problems at Wilson were mainly due to continued difficulties in golf club and ball sales, as well as lower sales and profitability in clothing and baseball products.
But Wilson would remain in all its current product areas, Amer said: "Wilson is maintaining its strong market position in all team sports product categories in the U.S."
With Wilson net sales only expected to increase marginally year on year, Amer said the unit's performance would be "clearly unprofitable."
While MacGregor Golf Company sales had been above target in the Asia-Pacific region, Amer said they fell short of expectations in the U.S. and Europe.

It forecast only a slight increase in MacGregor net sales this year, adding that losses were likely to remain at last year's level, when MacGregor booked an operating loss of 32 million markka ($7 million).
"Measures relating to the company's unprofitable operations are still being examined, and a final decision should have been made by the year end," Amer said.
Amer said its Atomic ski and skates unit, also headed for full-year losses, had suffered occasional delivery troubles throughout the year.

"The market for alpine ski equipment continues to decline," it said. Demand for cross-country skis was likely to remain stable but demand for snowboards would rise fast and Amer expected snowboard sales to double in 1996 from 1995.
It did not specify their 1995 level but Atomic's 1995 net sales totalled 674 million markka.
